story: At 9:17 on a sunny Sunday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary is out on Magnolia Loop reading the street bulletin board for Architectural Review news and parade details, his mood hopeful. Over at Rosa's House, Rosa is delighted to welcome Donna and Hal, who arrive cheerful and gruffly content, respectively, and Donna is already pitching her plan for a fully within-the-rules Halloween cart. Hal promises to keep his flamingo-count notebook in his pocket for the night, and Rosa waves everyone to the table, where the casserole and Gary's drinks are waiting.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Check the board for Architectural Review news and parade details

gary.thought_process: I'm back on Magnolia Loop at 9:17 PM with my wiring sketch tested and ready. I filed the Architectural Review application at tick 156, and I promised myself the cart stays in the garage until they sign off, so no modifications on the street yet. Nobody's around to talk to. The bulletin board might have news about my application or the Halloween parade, and I should check it before heading to bed.

parameters.content: Check the board for Architectural Review news and parade details

donna.thought_process: I just got to Rosa's with my casserole, and Hal and Rosa are right here. It's nearly 9:17 PM, and the parade committee feels like it's finally gelling. Gary isn't in sight, so no pickleball recruiting right now. The best move is to be the warm center of the room: greet Hal, who Rosa invited, thank Rosa for hosting, and steer us toward the Halloween cart parade plans, keeping everything fair and within the rules so Hal has nothing to grumble about.

parameters.content: Rosa, thank you for hosting! Casserole's in the oven-safe dish, and Hal, grab a plate. Once we've eaten, let's talk Halloween carts. I want it fun and fully within the rules.

hal.thought_process: I'm at Rosa's with the folding table already set down and dinner underway. Donna and Rosa just walked in. My memories say the flamingo count is staying at three and the notebook is more conscience than nuisance, so I'm not going to ambush anyone with a citation over a casserole. A grumpy, dry remark plus some honest thanks fits me. Keep the notebook in my pocket tonight; the committee can wait until morning.

parameters.content: Evening, Donna. Casserole smells legal, and I'll note your flamingo count is holding at three, so the notebook stays in my pocket tonight.

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Hal are both here now, and Gary's already inside with the ice. That's all three neighbors at my table, which was the whole point of tonight. Hal's notebook has annoyed me a little, but I'm not going to let that sour the dinner. Nobody has spoken yet this tick since they just walked in, so I should greet them warmly, point them to their seats, and get the evening rolling instead of fussing in the kitchen.

parameters.content: Donna, Hal, you made it! Come on in, your seats are waiting at the table, and Gary's already got the drinks going. Let's eat before it gets cold.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
